title: Related content: Partial-text indexing

judge.reasoning:
Patch B is the better fix.

**Correctness**
- B adds an opt-in `splitWords` option to the basic index type, which is exactly what the issue asks for (partial matching on e.g. `title`).
- Splitting uses `unicode.IsLetter`, `IsNumber` and `IsMark`, so non-ASCII text such as accented words and CJK is handled correctly.
- Keywords are deduplicated per document, so repeated words cannot inflate rank.
- It adds a `stopWords` list, which directly answers the issue's question about ignoring common words. The list can be configured per language, which addresses the i18n concern.
- `DecodeConfig` rejects `splitWords` on non-basic index types instead of misbehaving silently.

Patch A has a broader scope (tokenized fragments plus an `ApplyFilter` rewrite) with more risk:
- Tokenized fragment keywords are built through `stringToKeyword`, which returns a `StringKeyword`, not a `FragmentKeyword`.
- In `searchDate`, the `kw.(FragmentKeyword)` type assertion therefore never succeeds for tokenized words. `ff.words` stays empty, and the new heading filter appears to be dead code. Its `ApplyFilter` test looks likely to fail or to pass only by accident.
- On the basic path, A's `ToKeywords` does not deduplicate tokens, so repeated words over-weight a document.
- A offers only `MinTokenLength` as a crude stand-in for stop words.
- Whitespace-based splitting with punctuation trimming leaves hyphenated or joined words unsplit.

**Tests**
- B has focused unit tests (keyword splitting, stop words, non-ASCII input, search, config validation) and an integration test that checks a split index alongside an unsplit one.
- A has more integration tests, but they cover the riskier fragments path, including the questionable `ApplyFilter` behavior.

**Scope and craft**
- A includes unrelated whitespace churn in existing tests.
- B updates the docs and keeps the change small and coherent by routing through a single `stringsToKeywords` helper.

issue_md:
When specifying the indices for related content, it would be useful to specify that some of them were split by word, so that their text could be matched partially. This would allow the title to be used for more in-depth indexing, rather than requiring the user to specify tags / keywords.

This would likely increase memory usage and decrease performance, so should definitely be opt-in!

I suspect common words (a, an, the etc) might want to be ignored? Although doing that in a sane, i18n-friendly manner might be a challenge!

+// stringsToKeywords converts the given strings to keywords, splitting
+// them into words if configured to do so.
+func (cfg IndexConfig) stringsToKeywords(s ...string) []Keyword {
+	if !cfg.SplitWords {
+		kw := make([]Keyword, len(s))
+		for i := range s {
+			kw[i] = cfg.stringToKeyword(s[i])
+		}
+		return kw
+	}
+
+	var kw []Keyword
+	seen := make(map[Keyword]bool)
+	for _, ss := range s {
+		for _, word := range splitWords(ss) {
+			if cfg.isStopWord(word) {
+				continue
+			}
+			k := cfg.stringToKeyword(word)
+			if seen[k] {
+				continue
+			}
+			seen[k] = true
+			kw = append(kw, k)
+		}
+	}
+	return kw
+}
+
+func (cfg IndexConfig) isStopWord(word string) bool {
+	for _, sw := range cfg.StopWords {
+		if strings.EqualFold(sw, word) {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// splitWords splits s into words, treating any rune that is not a letter,
+// a number or a combining mark as a separator.
+func splitWords(s string) []string {
+	return strings.FieldsFunc(s, func(r rune) bool {
+		return !unicode.IsLetter(r) && !unicode.IsNumber(r) && !unicode.IsMark(r)
+	})
+}

+func TestToKeywordsSplitWords(t *testing.T) {
+	c := qt.New(t)
+
+	config := IndexConfig{SplitWords: true, ToLower: true, StopWords: []string{"a", "The", "OF"}}
+
+	keywords, err := config.ToKeywords("The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King")
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(keywords, qt.DeepEquals, []Keyword{
+		StringKeyword("lord"),
+		StringKeyword("rings"),
+		StringKeyword("return"),
+		StringKeyword("king"),
+	})
+
+	keywords, err = config.ToKeywords([]any{"Hugo is fast", "Go-templates, a.k.a. Go"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(keywords, qt.DeepEquals, []Keyword{
+		StringKeyword("hugo"),
+		StringKeyword("is"),
+		StringKeyword("fast"),
+		StringKeyword("go"),
+		StringKeyword("templates"),
+		StringKeyword("k"),
+	})
+
+	// Non-ASCII text.
+	keywords, err = IndexConfig{SplitWords: true}.ToKeywords("Größe und café, 日本語")
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(keywords, qt.DeepEquals, []Keyword{
+		StringKeyword("Größe"),
+		StringKeyword("und"),
+		StringKeyword("café"),
+		StringKeyword("日本語"),
+	})
+
+	// Not enabled: the full string is the keyword.
+	keywords, err = IndexConfig{StopWords: []string{"the"}}.ToKeywords("The Lord of the Rings")
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(keywords, qt.DeepEquals, []Keyword{StringKeyword("The Lord of the Rings")})
+}
+
+func TestSearchSplitWords(t *testing.T) {
+	c := qt.New(t)
+	cfg := Config{

+	idx := NewInvertedIndex(cfg)
+	docs := []Document{

+	if strings.IndexFunc(title, unicode.IsSpace) == -1 && strings.IndexByte(title, '&') == -1 {
+		title = strings.TrimFunc(html.UnescapeString(title), func(r rune) bool { return !unicode.IsLetter(r) && !unicode.IsDigit(r) })
+		if title == "" {
+			return nil
+		}
+		return []string{title}
+	}
+	raw := strings.Fields(html.UnescapeString(title))
+	words := raw[:0]
+	for _, w := range raw {
+		w = strings.TrimFunc(w, func(r rune) bool { return !unicode.IsLetter(r) && !unicode.IsDigit(r) })
+		if w != "" {
+			words = append(words, w)
+		}
+	}
+	if len(words) == 0 {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return words
+}

title: resources/images: Poor overlay quality when background image is an indexed (not true color) PNG

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the root cause the same way: they skip re-quantizing the output to the source palette when filters can add new colors. That is what clamps an Overlay onto an indexed PNG to the background's 256 colors. Both update the paletted overlay.png and text.png golden images to match.

Patch B is more precise. It still keeps the source palette when every filter is geometric (images.Process specs or orientation filters). It drops the palette only when a color-introducing filter such as Overlay, Text, Padding or Grayscale is present. Patch A drops palette preservation for every `Filter` call, so `$img.Filter (images.Process "resize 100x")` or AutoOrient on an indexed PNG now loses its palette. That is an unnecessary behavior regression relative to the plain Resize path.

Patch A also bundles a separate change for a different issue (12536). It switches hex color parsing from RGBA to NRGBA and rewrites ColorGoToHexString, Color.init and AddColorToPalette. This alters semantics beyond the issue and changes an unrelated golden image (padding-transparent-chained.png). That adds risk and obscures the fix.

On tests, Patch B adds a targeted integration test. It checks pixel by pixel that the overlay keeps the foreground's colors and that the text color and padding color are preserved. It checks that grayscale output is truly gray and that a purely geometric Process still yields a paletted image. This test would fail before the fix. Patch A's test changes are mostly about the unrelated hex/NRGBA work, and it relies on golden-image updates for the actual issue.

B is more correct, better tested and better scoped.

title: Automatic summary may generate invalid HTML with blockquotes and lists

judge.reasoning:
Both patches move the summary cut-off forward when it falls inside an open element, which fixes the reported blockquote and list leak. They differ in which elements trigger that expansion.

Patch B balances every open element, including generic wrapper `div`s. AsciiDoc output nests content in `sect1`/`sectionbody` divs, Org mode in `outline-*` divs, and Markdown authors often wrap a whole post in a raw `<div class="post">`. In each of those cases Patch B would extend the summary to the end of the section or even the whole document. That is a substantial behavioral regression: summaries could silently become the entire content.

Patch A limits expansion to the element types the issue is about (`blockquote`, `ul`, `ol`, `dl`, `table`), anchored to the outermost such element open at the cut point. It also absorbs directly-following end tags such as the AsciiDoc `quoteblock` wrapper div, and keeps the original cut if the element is never closed. Its tests explicitly cover the regression risks Patch B misses:
- Org outline wrappers and a plain div wrapper are not expanded.
- Nested AsciiDoc sections are handled.
- Wrapped reStructuredText output (the `<div class="document">` case) is handled.
- Nested blockquotes, lists with void elements, and unclosed blockquotes are handled.

Patch A also adds an integration test that reproduces the issue end to end.

Patch A uses the robust `x/net/html` tokenizer. Patch B hand-rolls a scanner, which adds surface for edge-case bugs. Patch B also rewrites the existing benchmark, dropping its correctness assertions and switching from `b.Loop` to `b.N`. That is unrelated churn that weakens existing checks.

Overall Patch A is more correct and targeted, and better tested.

hugo v0.151.0+extended+withdeploy darwin/arm64 BuildDate=2025-10-02T13:30:36Z VendorInfo=brew
### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes ## Issue Using a blockquote that extends past the `.Summary` cutoff causes the content below `{{ .Summary }}` to be treated as part of the blockquote until the end of the parent tag. [Reproduction repo](https://github.com/imomaliev/hugo-blockquote-summary-leak) Hugo's `.Summary` may lead to `blockquote` end tag be below cutoff point ## Explanation In most modern browsers this html code will be parsed and rendered without errors ```html

1

``` Leading to shown in browser as a source ```html

1

``` This is due to [these parsing rules](html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inbody#:~:text=An%20end%20tag%20whose%20tag%20name%20is%20one%20of%3A%20%22address%22%2C%20%22article%22%2C%20%22aside%22%2C%20%22blockquote%22) > An end tag whose tag name is one of: "address", "article", "aside", "blockquote", "button", "center", "details", "dialog", "dir", "div", "dl", "fieldset", "figcaption", "figure", "footer", "header", "hgroup", "listing", "main", "menu", "nav", "ol", "pre", "search", "section", "select", "summary", "ul" > > If the stack of open elements does not have an element in scope that is an HTML element with the same tag name as that of the token, then this is a parse error; ignore the token. > > Otherwise, run these steps: > > Generate implied end tags. > > If the current node is not an HTML element with the same tag name as that of the token, then this is a parse error. > > Pop elements from the stack of open elements until an HTML element with the same tag name as the token has been popped from the stack. ## To Discuss I think the best case scenario is for `.Summary` to handle generation of implied tags. But I am not sure how to do that myself. For now I plan to provide a PR with fixes for a theme and docs, to avoid confusion and errors - https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/14045 - https://github.com/gohugoio/hugoDocs/pull/3230

title: Support slug in section, taxonomy, and term pages

judge.reasoning:
Patch A does not address the issue at all. It renames an interface parameter and swaps HasAnyVector for HasVector in MatchSiteVector. That is unrelated churn, and possibly a semantic change, with no connection to slug support for sections, taxonomies or terms. It adds no tests.

Patch B targets the slug feature directly. The repository apparently already has base slug support, since the existing test in page_permalink_test.go expects /es/ayuda/ paths. Patch B fixes what is still missing for live rebuilds. It tracks a per-branch slug signature tree, compares that tree against the previous build, and forces affected descendants to be rebuilt from source and their identities marked changed. It also fixes two latent bugs that the rebuild path exposes: contentNodesMap unpacking of page meta sources, and aliasing of the term sitesMatrixBase map (fixed with maps.Clone).

Patch B adds several meaningful rebuild tests covering:
- section slug edits that propagate to descendants, resources and terms
- taxonomy slug edits
- cascade terms without a content file
- a slug edit combined with adding a new language
- a slug edit combined with a cascade edit

It also adjusts one existing assertion to the absolute RSS link. That adjustment is slightly suspicious, but it is plausible for an index.xml <link> to carry the baseURL.

Patch B is clearly the better fix.

issue_md:
<!-- Describe this new feature. Think about if it really belongs in the Hugo core module; you may want to discuss it on https://discourse.gohugo.io/ first.  -->

Currently with multilanguage sites you can localize the URL for pages by setting `slug` in the frontmatter.

However there is no `slug` support for sections. This means the only way to localize a section URL is to use `url` together with `[[cascade]]`. This is annoying since you have to "redo from scratch" the entire URL format, with `:` tokens, duplicating names for parent sections, etc.

Proposal: add support for `slug` in section pages. It would behave the obvious way, basically being equivalent to changing the directory name for the section. It would affect the URL for the section and all descendant pages.

Example:

```
help/
    _index.en.md    # contains no slug
    _index.es.md    # contains slug="ayuda"
    how-to-frob/
       index.en.md    # contains no slug
       index.es.md    # contains slug="como-frobear"
```

would result in the following paths:

```
help/
help/how-to-frob/
es/ayuda/
es/ayuda/como-frobear/
```

title: Make default baseUrl https://example.org/
issue_md:
If I want to create a very basic site, the only reason I currently need to create a config file is to set the `baseUrl`.

So, having the `baseURL` default to https://example.org/  would be a slightly breaking change, but it would solve more issues than it introduces.

title: Add build.cleanDestinationDir config option

judge.reasoning:
Both patches add a `build.cleanDestinationDir` struct with an enable switch and glob-based retention matched against publishDir-relative paths. Both would let the reporter keep `.git`, `.domains`, `_redirects` and `foo/bar/.mysecretfile`.

**Patch B** is the safer fix.
- It adds a single `retain` list on top of the existing hardcoded protections, which still preserve `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes` and dot-directories.
- The root `cleanDestinationDir` key and the `--cleanDestinationDir` flag keep working unchanged: the build decoder ORs them into `Enable`.
- It also accepts the bool shorthand `build.cleanDestinationDir = true`, including from env vars.
- Its glob compilation is explicit, uses '/' as the separator, normalizes leading slashes, and wraps errors with the option name.
- Tests:
  - A unit test covers decoding (bool, bool-string and map forms), matching semantics (root-only versus `**` patterns, nested paths) and invalid-glob errors.
  - A new testscript covers the issue's exact scenario: enabled via config with no static dir, enabled via flag with a static dir, the bool form, and the disabled case.
- Docs are updated.

**Patch A** is a broader redesign that adds risk without adding value for the issue.
- It deprecates the root `cleanDestinationDir` key.
- It reroutes the CLI flag through `keyMap` to a nested dotted key, `build.cleanDestinationDir.enable`, which depends on nested Set semantics working for flags.
- It replaces the hardcoded keep logic with default `keepFiles`/`keepDirs` globs. Any user who sets `keepFiles` silently loses the default protection for `.gitignore`/`.gitattributes` and dot-dirs; its own scenario 4 output shows `.gitignore` and `.hidden/` being deleted. That is a surprising behavior regression for anyone adopting the new option.
- Its negation semantics (`! **.html` meaning 'keep everything except html') make the keep list double as a delete list, which is harder to reason about.
- It does add `.git` files to the defaults, which helps the worktree case, and its testscript coverage is reasonable.
- It has no unit tests and no docs.

On balance, B resolves the issue with less risk, preserves backward compatibility, and has more thorough tests.

issue_md:
<!-- Describe this new feature. Think about if it really belongs in the Hugo core module; you may want to discuss it on https://discourse.gohugo.io/ first.  -->

## Usecase

I'm using Codeberg Pages to host my website, you can find the repostitory at https://codeberg.org/ilovelinux/pages

I have two branches:
- `main`: hugo project
- `pages`: hugo build (output of `public/`)

Since I'm using Codeberg Pages with a custom domain, I also need a `.domains` file[^codebergDomains] to be pushed in the `pages` branch.

### When I

- Have files in the `static/` directory.
- Switch to `main` branch.
- Create the `public/` folder using a git worktree of the `pages` branch.
- Run `hugo build --cleanDestinationDir`.

### I need

- To remove outdated content
- To retain:
  - `.git` **file** created by `git worktree`[^gitWorktreeFile].
  - `.domains` **file** used by Codeberg Pages in order to allow custom domains[^codebergDomains].
  - `_redirects` **file** for redirects (however I'm not using it yet)[^codebergRedirects].

### Instead

- The files I need to be retained are deleted.

## Proposal

Add a configuration field to list relative file paths to `public/` that should be retained when using `--cleanDestinationDir`.

#### Example
```yaml
 filesToRetain:
  - .git
  - .domains
  - _redirects
  - foo/bar/.mysecretfile
```

Files retained:
- `public/.git`
- `public/.domains`
- `public/_redirects`
- `public/foo/bar/.mysecretfile`

> [!NOTE]
> I'm not suggesting to use `filesToRetain` as configuration field, but I couldn't think of a better name.

## Notes

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `--cleanDestinationDir` does nothing when when the `static/` directory doesn't exist since its value is used inside the `copyStaticTo` function.
> https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/c4bbc2805c7092deafabae01e71ff2dda37bd877/commands/hugobuilder.go#L481

### Workaround

> [!WARNING]
> This approach is error-prone.

I implemented a workaround in my [Makefile](https://codeberg.org/ilovelinux/pages/src/commit/072c6dc048096c98c3422e824cb1d3bbc0b60736/Makefile#L9-L11) that:
- Repairs the worktree folder, as suggested in https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/6261#issuecomment-1692321365.
- Restores the `.domains` file.

### Related issues & PR
- https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/3202 was about `.git` **folder** being deleted.
  Fixed thanks to:
  - https://github.com/spf13/fsync/pull/10
  - https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/3210.
- https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/4546 was about `.git` **file** of a submodule[^gitSubmoduleFile] being deleted. Closed because it was considered a discussion.
- https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/6261 was introducing a fix for the `.git` **file** in order to work correctly with git worktrees and submodules. Closed because of the Stale bot but it looks like it was still kept into consideration since @bep kept moving it among milestones after that.
  However this wouldn't solve my issue since `.domains` and `_redirects` files would still be deleted.

[^codebergDomains]: https://docs.codeberg.org/codeberg-pages/using-custom-domain/
[^codebergRedirects]: https://docs.codeberg.org/codeberg-pages/redirects/

title: metrics: --templateMetrics duration columns have inconsistent formatting

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the issue the same way. Each adds a formatDuration helper that picks s/ms/µs/ns, prints two fixed decimals, and pads the unit to a fixed width, so decimal points line up in the right-aligned %15s/%12s columns. Go's fmt width counts runes, so the multibyte 'µ' does not break alignment in either patch. Correctness is therefore essentially equal.

Tests decide it.
- Patch A unit-tests formatDuration across all unit boundaries, including 0, 999ns, the µs/ms/s ranges, and the padded 's '. It also adds TestWriteMetricsAlignedDurations, which drives WriteMetrics in both hints and no-hints modes with rows of mixed magnitudes. That test checks sort order and asserts that the rune positions of the decimal points match in every row. This directly tests the issue's requirement, and it would fail against the old time.Duration.String() output.
- Patch B only unit-tests formatDuration with four values and never checks alignment in the actual table.

Scope:
- Patch A keeps the number and unit adjacent ('1.50µs', '1.00s '), which matches the issue's 'unit suffix padded' wording. The existing partials integration test regex still matches this output, so no other tests need to change.
- Patch B inserts a space between the number and the unit, which forced it to change the regex in tpl/partials/partials_integration_test.go. The change is small but adds churn.

Craft is comparable; A's single Sprintf with a computed divisor and unit is slightly cleaner. Overall, A is better on tests and slightly better on scope.

issue_md:
The `--templateMetrics` output table prints duration values (sum/avg/max) using `time.Duration.String()`, which varies both units and decimal places depending on the magnitude. This makes the table hard to scan when rows have durations of different magnitudes.

**Proposed fix:** Use a fixed-decimal formatter (two decimal places, unit suffix padded to consistent width) so decimal points align across all rows in the table.

title: Make .Render take additional data

judge.reasoning:
Both patches make the same core change. Each widens `Render` to `...any`, updates every implementer (pageContentOutput, LazyContentProvider, nopPage, testPage), and passes the optional data as the template context instead of the Page. Template resolution stays keyed to the page's content type in both.

Correctness: the issue writes the signature as `PAGE.Render [DATA] NAME`, with data first. Patch A accepts both `NAME DATA` and `DATA NAME` through `parseRenderArgs`. It tells them apart by which argument is a string, and if both are strings it treats the first as the name. Patch B accepts only `NAME [CONTEXT]`. Calling it in the order the issue shows, e.g. `.Render (dict ...) "lid"`, makes B try to cast a map to a string and fail. Patch A therefore covers the scenario the issue describes, and Patch B misses half of it.

Edge handling: Patch A rejects non-string layout names such as `42`, rejects an empty name, and limits the call to two arguments, each with a clear error. Patch B checks the argument count but uses `cast.ToStringE`, so a numeric name is silently accepted as "42". When the data argument is nil, Patch A falls back to the Page. That choice is debatable but defensible, and it is tested.

Tests: Patch A tests both argument orders and confirms that a content-type-specific layout (`books/lid.html`) is still chosen when data is passed. It also covers string data, nil data, and five error cases. Patch B's tests are thinner: one data case using a dict that imitates a Title field, and two error cases. Both sets of tests would fail without their fix.

Scope/craft: Patch A also updates the user docs to describe the new argument, which is reasonable because the feature is user-facing. Its code keeps parsing separate from execution and is cleaner for that. Patch B is shorter, but it renames the concept to "view" in its error messages, which doesn't match the existing "layout" wording.

Overall, Patch A matches the issue's stated syntax, handles more edge cases, and is better tested.

issue_md:
See https://gohugo.io/methods/page/render/#article
See #15076

> PAGE.Render NAME

This has been discussed before. 

* The contract has always been that the templates that `.Renders` gets the data context as e.g. `page.html`, a `page.Page`.
* We can only pass 1 argument to Go's template renderer, which I guess is the blocking reason for not having done this sooner.

So, if we want to do:

> PAGE.Render [DATA] NAME

I'm guessing we have 2 top-level options:

* We say that if `DATA` is set, we use that as the context passed to the templates,. else `PAGE`.
* We somehow (e.g. by embeding it in a `{ DataAdditionalContext, Page }` struct or  putting it into the current `context.Context`) wrap the `Page` so you can do both `.RelPermalink` and `.DataAdditionalContext` (naming of the latter is just picked out of a hat without thinking too hard.

title: Add importContext to resources.Copy

judge.reasoning:
The issue asks for `importContext` to be added to `resources.Copy`, stored internally on the resource, and then honored by css.Build, js.Build/Batch, css.Sass and TailwindCSS.

**Patch A does this directly.**
- It extends `resources.Copy` to take an optional string or options map with `targetPath` and `importContext`, and makes the target path optional, as the issue proposes.
- It stores the context in an unexported field on `genericResource`, following the issue's `Internal*` hint via `InternalResourceImportContext`.
- It exposes the context through `ResourceTransformationCtx.ImportContext`.
- It wires that context into the CSS inline-import resolver (PostCSS/Tailwind), esbuild (js.Build/css.Build), js.Batch (as a fallback), libsass and dartsass.
- It handles cache correctness by adding an import-context key to the resource `Key()`. That key includes a content hash for resources such as `FromString`.
- It validates bad input with a clear error message.
- Its integration tests cover: css.Build with media queries, page resources in js.Build with Mount, same target path with different contexts, same path with different content, a transformed resource, rebuild on edit, error cases, js.Batch, and both Sass transpilers.

**Patch B does not implement the requested API.**
- It adds `importContext` as an option on each transformer (css.Build, css.Sass, TailwindCSS) and leaves `resources.Copy` untouched.
- It carries considerable unrelated and risky churn:
  - bumps hashstructure to v1.0.0 and rewrites the hashing internals;
  - removes `pageState.Key` and adds `pageOutput.Key`;
  - changes `Color.Hash` to `Key`;
  - removes `resourceGetterFunc` and support for function getters;
  - changes the key semantics of `FromString`;
  - adds a new `testinginternal` template namespace.
- Its hash test asserts brittle hard-coded hash values.
- Its js.Build support lacks error-message and source-map handling.

On correctness against the stated ask, scope, and risk, Patch A is clearly better.

title: Add css.ChromaStyles

judge.reasoning:
Both patches move the CLI generation logic into a shared markup/highlight function, refactor `hugo gen chromastyles` to use it, and add a `css.ChromaStyles` template function. Both produce essentially identical CSS. They differ mainly in how the Resource is created and how options are handled.

Correctness and fit to the issue:
- The issue says resource creation should be delegated to `create.Client.FromString`. Patch B does exactly that, so it inherits create's caching, publishing and dependency tracking.
- Patch A builds the resource directly with `ResourceSpec.NewResource` and `GroupIdentity: identity.Anonymous`, plus its own 10-entry hash cache. This bypasses the requested path. The anonymous identity can weaken change tracking and rebuild behavior.
- Patch A does have one nice touch: the style defaults to `markup.highlight.style`. That goes beyond the ask.
- Patch A decodes with `WeakDecode`, which silently ignores misspelled options.
- Patch B rejects unknown keys with a clear error, normalizes `targetPath` (it trims the leading slash and treats "/" as empty), and wraps errors with a `css.ChromaStyles:` prefix.

Tests:
- Patch B adds unit tests for `DecodeOptions` and `Generate`.
- Its integration tests cover merging options from `site.Params`, the media type, highlightStyle, omitClassComments, the default style, and a broader error table (unknown option, slash-only targetPath, empty style).
- Patch A's integration tests and benchmark are thinner.

Scope and craft:
- Patch B adds documentation and exposes a `DefaultStyle` constant that the CLI flag shares.
- Patch B's separate `chromastyles` package is clean.

Overall, Patch B follows the issue's explicit design guidance and is more robust and better tested.

issue_md:
We have a [CLI command](https://gohugo.io/commands/hugo_gen_chromastyles/#hugo-gen-chromastyles) for this, with Chroma's recent addition of dark/light modes, it would be convenient to generate these on-the-fly. This would allow this to be configured in `hugo.toml` and also allow the user an easier way to find the correct settings.

E.g.

```handlebars
{{ $dark := css.ChromaStyles dict 
  "targetPath" "css/croma_dark.css"
   "style" "monokai"
   "modeSelector" "dark"
    "mode" "dark"
}}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ $dark.RelPermalink }}">
```

This would be even more useful if we fix #15103.


* The options would be `targetPath` + the options in https://gohugo.io/commands/hugo_gen_chromastyles/#hugo-gen-chromastyles
* Some sharing of code between the gen command in the commands package would be sensible.
* Creating the `Resource` should be delegated to `create.Client.FromString`.

+---
+title: css.ChromaStyles
+description: Returns a CSS resource containing a stylesheet for the Chroma syntax highlighter.
+categories: []
+keywords: []
+params:
+  functions_and_methods:
+    aliases: []
+    returnType: resource.Resource
+    signatures: [css.ChromaStyles OPTIONS]
+---
+
+{{< new-in 0.165.0 />}}
+
+Use the `css.ChromaStyles` function to generate a syntax highlighting stylesheet when `markup.highlight.noClasses` is disabled in your project configuration. It is the template equivalent of the [`hugo gen chromastyles`][] command.
+
+```go-html-template
+{{ $opts := dict
+  "targetPath" "css/chroma_dark.css"
+  "style" "github"
+  "mode" "dark"
+  "modeSelector" true
+}}
+{{ with css.ChromaStyles $opts }}
+  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ .RelPermalink }}">
+{{ end }}
+```
+
+## Options
+
+targetPath
+: (`string`) The publish path of the stylesheet, relative to the `publishDir`. Required.
+
+style
+: (`string`) The name of the Chroma style. See the [syntax highlighting styles][] for a preview of the available styles. Default is `friendly`.
+
+mode
+: (`string`) The style mode, either `light` or `dark`. Returns an error if the style does not have the given mode.
+
+modeSelector
+: (`bool`) Whether to scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. `.dark .chroma`, allowing you to toggle light and dark stylesheets with a class on a parent element. Default is `false`.
+
+highlightStyle
+: (`string`) Foreground and background colors for highlighted lines, e.g. `#fff000 bg:#000fff`.
+
+lineNumbersInlineStyle
+: (`string`) Foreground and background colors for inline line numbers, e.g. `#fff000 bg:#000fff`.
+
+lineNumbersTableStyle
+: (`string`) Foreground and background colors for table line numbers, e.g. `#fff000 bg:#000fff`.
+
+omitClassComments
+: (`bool`) Whether to omit CSS class comment prefixes in the generated CSS. Default is `false`.
+
+[`hugo gen chromastyles`]: /commands/hugo_gen_chromastyles/
+[syntax highlighting styles]: /quick-reference/syntax-highlighting-styles/

@@ -0,0 +1,195 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Hugo Authors. All rights reserved.
+//

+// you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.

+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+// Package chromastyles generates CSS stylesheets for the Chroma code highlighter.
+// It is shared by the hugo gen chromastyles command and the css.ChromaStyles template function.
+package chromastyles
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"fmt"
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/formatters/html"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/styles"
+	"github.com/mitchellh/mapstructure"
+)
+
+// DefaultStyle is the default Chroma style.
+const DefaultStyle = "friendly"
+
+// Options configures the generated stylesheet.
+type Options struct {
+	// The Chroma style name, e.g. "monokai".
+	Style string
+
+	// The style mode, "light" or "dark". Optional.
+	Mode string
+
+	// Scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+	ModeSelector bool
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for highlighted lines, e.g. "#fff000 bg:#000fff".
+	HighlightStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for inline line numbers.
+	LineNumbersInlineStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for table line numbers.
+	LineNumbersTableStyle string
+
+	// Omit CSS class comment prefixes in the generated CSS.
+	OmitClassComments bool
+}
+
+// DecodeOptions decodes m into Options, applying defaults.
+// Keys are matched case-insensitively.
+func DecodeOptions(m map[string]any) (Options, error) {
+	opts := Options{Style: DefaultStyle}
+	if m == nil {
+		return opts, nil
+	}
+	var md mapstructure.Metadata
+	decoder, err := mapstructure.NewDecoder(&mapstructure.DecoderConfig{
+		WeaklyTypedInput: true,
+		Metadata:         &md,
+		Result:           &opts,
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return opts, err
+	}
+	if err := decoder.Decode(m); err != nil {
+		return opts, err
+	}
+	if len(md.Unused) > 0 {
+		slices.Sort(md.Unused)
+		return opts, fmt.Errorf("unknown option(s): %s", strings.Join(md.Unused, ", "))
+	}
+	return opts, nil
+}
+
+// Generate generates a CSS stylesheet for the given options.
+func Generate(opts Options) (string, error) {
+	styleName := strings.ToLower(opts.Style)
+	if !slices.Contains(styles.Names(), styleName) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid style: %s", styleName)
+	}
+
+	var chromaStyle *chroma.Style
+	if opts.Mode != "" {
+		var chromaMode chroma.Mode
+		switch opts.Mode {
+		case "light":
+			chromaMode = chroma.Light
+		case "dark":
+			chromaMode = chroma.Dark
+		default:
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid mode: %s", opts.Mode)
+		}
+
+		chromaStyle = styles.GetForMode(styleName, chromaMode)
+		if chromaStyle.Mode() != chromaMode {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a %q mode", styleName, opts.Mode)
+		}
+	} else {
+		chromaStyle = styles.Get(styleName)
+	}
+	builder := chromaStyle.Builder()
+	if opts.HighlightStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineHighlight, opts.HighlightStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbers, opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersTableStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbersTable, opts.LineNumbersTableStyle)
+	}
+	style, err := builder.Build()
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+
+	options := []html.Option{
+		html.WithCSSComments(!opts.OmitClassComments),
+	}
+	if !opts.ModeSelector {
+		// Only needed for the shared-scope overlay; ModeSelector
+		// gives each mode its own scope and makes this redundant.
+		options = append(options, html.WithCustomCSS(cssOverrides(style)))
+	}
+
+	formatter := html.New(options...)
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	if err := formatter.WriteCSS(&buf, style); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	css := buf.String()
+	if opts.ModeSelector {
+		// Scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+		// This allows generating both light and dark stylesheets and toggling
+		// them with a parent class on the page.
+		// There's no upstream option for this (I think), so do string replacements for now.
+		// TODO(bep) upstream option for this.
+		var prefix string
+		switch style.Mode() {
+		case chroma.Light:
+			prefix = ".light "
+		case chroma.Dark:
+			prefix = ".dark "
+		default:
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a %q mode", style.Name, opts.Mode)
+		}
+		replacer := strings.NewReplacer(
+			".bg {", prefix+".bg {",
+			".chroma ", prefix+".chroma ",
+		)
+		css = replacer.Replace(css)
+	}
+
+	return css, nil
+}
+
+// cssOverrides re-emits leaf token colors that Chroma's minifier drops
+// because they equal the style's default foreground (the .chroma color). Without
+// modeSelector scoping, a paired light/dark stylesheet shares the same .chroma
+// scope, and the light sheet's explicit rule (e.g. .chroma .nx) would otherwise
+// leak into dark mode, since an explicit declaration beats inheritance.
+func cssOverrides(style *chroma.Style) map[chroma.TokenType]string {
+	bg := style.Get(chroma.Background)
+	m := make(map[chroma.TokenType]string)
+	for tt := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if tt == chroma.Background || !style.Has(tt) || !leafToken(tt) {
+			continue
+		}
+		entry := style.Get(tt)
+		if !entry.Sub(bg).IsZero() || !entry.Colour.IsSet() {
+			continue
+		}
+		if css := html.StyleEntryToCSS(chroma.StyleEntry{Colour: entry.Colour}); css != "" {
+			m[tt] = css
+		}
+	}
+	return m
+}
+
+func leafToken(tt chroma.TokenType) bool {
+	for other := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if other != tt && (other.Category() == tt || other.SubCategory() == tt) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}

+func TestDecodeOptions(t *testing.T) {
+	c := qt.New(t)
+
+	opts, err := DecodeOptions(nil)
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(opts, qt.DeepEquals, Options{Style: DefaultStyle})
+
+	opts, err = DecodeOptions(map[string]any{
+		"style":                  "monokai",
+		"MODE":                   "dark",
+		"modeSelector":           "true",
+		"highlightStyle":         "#fff",
+		"lineNumbersInlineStyle": "#aaa",
+		"lineNumbersTableStyle":  "#bbb",
+		"omitClassComments":      true,
+	})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(opts, qt.DeepEquals, Options{
+		Style:                  "monokai",
+		Mode:                   "dark",
+		ModeSelector:           true,
+		HighlightStyle:         "#fff",
+		LineNumbersInlineStyle: "#aaa",
+		LineNumbersTableStyle:  "#bbb",
+		OmitClassComments:      true,
+	})
+
+	_, err = DecodeOptions(map[string]any{"foo": "bar"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, "unknown option\\(s\\): foo")
+}
+
+func TestGenerate(t *testing.T) {
+	c := qt.New(t)
+
+	css, err := Generate(Options{Style: "github-dark"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	// Same-colour token classes are kept when not scoped by mode selector.
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Matches, `(?s).*NameOther.*\.chroma \.nx \{ color:#e6edf3 \}.*`)
+
+	css, err = Generate(Options{Style: "ashen", ModeSelector: true})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Contains, ".dark .chroma ")
+
+	css, err = Generate(Options{Style: "monokai", OmitClassComments: true})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Not(qt.Contains), "GenericSubheading")
+
+	_, err = Generate(Options{Style: "__invalid_style__"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, "invalid style: __invalid_style__")
+	_, err = Generate(Options{Style: ""})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, "invalid style: ")
+	_, err = Generate(Options{Style: "friendly", Mode: "dark"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, `style "friendly" does not have a "dark" mode`)
+}

+func TestChromaStyles(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	files := `
+-- hugo.toml --
+disableKinds = ["page", "section", "taxonomy", "term", "sitemap", "rss"]
+[params.chroma]
+style = "github"
+mode = "dark"
+modeSelector = true
+-- layouts/home.html --
+{{ $dark := css.ChromaStyles (merge site.Params.chroma (dict "targetPath" "css/chroma_dark.css")) }}
+{{ $light := css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "/css/chroma_light.css" "style" "github" "mode" "light" "modeSelector" true) }}
+{{ $plain := css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "css/chroma_plain.css" "style" "Monokai" "omitClassComments" true "highlightStyle" "#fff000 bg:#000fff") }}
+{{ $default := css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "css/chroma_default.css") }}
+Dark: {{ $dark.RelPermalink }}|{{ $dark.MediaType }}|
+Light: {{ $light.RelPermalink }}|
+Plain: {{ $plain.RelPermalink }}|
+Default: {{ $default.RelPermalink }}|
+`
+
+	b := hugolib.Test(t, files)
+
+	b.AssertFileContent("public/index.html",
+		"Dark: /css/chroma_dark.css|text/css|",
+		"Light: /css/chroma_light.css|",
+		"Plain: /css/chroma_plain.css|",
+		"Default: /css/chroma_default.css|",
+	)
+	b.AssertFileContent("public/css/chroma_dark.css", "/* Background */ .dark .bg {", ".dark .chroma ", "! Generated using")
+	b.AssertFileContent("public/css/chroma_light.css", ".light .chroma ", "! .dark ")
+	b.AssertFileContent("public/css/chroma_plain.css", ".chroma .hl { color:#fff000;background-color:#000fff }", "! /* LineHighlight */", "! .dark ", "! .light ")
+	// friendly is the default style.
+	b.AssertFileContent("public/css/chroma_default.css", "/* Background */ .bg { background-color:#f0f0f0; }")
+}
+
+func TestChromaStylesErrors(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	for _, test := range []struct {
+		name     string
+		template string
+		expected string
+	}{
+		{"no targetPath", `{{ css.ChromaStyles (dict "style" "monokai") }}`, "targetPath must be set"},
+		{"slash-only targetPath", `{{ css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "/") }}`, "targetPath must be set"},
+		{"empty style", `{{ css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "a.css" "style" "") }}`, "invalid style: "},
+		{"invalid style", `{{ css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "a.css" "style" "__invalid_style__") }}`, "invalid style: __invalid_style__"},
+		{"invalid mode", `{{ css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "a.css" "style" "github" "mode" "dim") }}`, "invalid mode: dim"},
+		{"missing mode", `{{ css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "a.css" "style" "friendly" "mode" "dark") }}`, `style "friendly" does not have a "dark" mode`},
+		{"unknown option", `{{ css.ChromaStyles (dict "targetPath" "a.css" "styel" "monokai") }}`, "unknown option(s): styel"},
+	} {
+		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			t.Parallel()
+			files := `
+-- hugo.toml --
+disableKinds = ["page", "section", "taxonomy", "term", "sitemap", "rss"]
+-- layouts/home.html --
+` + test.template + "\n"
+			b, err := hugolib.TestE(t, files)
+			b.Assert(err, qt.IsNotNil)
+			b.Assert(err.Error(), qt.Contains, test.expected)
+		})
+	}
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,161 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Hugo Authors. All rights reserved.
+//
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+// you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.

+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+package highlight
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"fmt"
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/formatters/html"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/styles"
+)
+
+// ChromaStylesOptions holds options for ChromaStylesCSS.
+type ChromaStylesOptions struct {
+	// Highlighter style, e.g. "monokai".
+	Style string
+
+	// Style mode, "light" or "dark".
+	Mode string
+
+	// Scope selectors under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+	ModeSelector bool
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for highlighted lines, e.g. "#fff000 bg:#000fff".
+	HighlightStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for inline line numbers.
+	LineNumbersInlineStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for table line numbers.
+	LineNumbersTableStyle string
+
+	// Omit CSS class comment prefixes in the generated CSS.
+	OmitClassComments bool
+}
+
+// ChromaStylesCSS generates a CSS stylesheet for the Chroma code highlighter.
+// This stylesheet is needed if markup.highlight.noClasses is disabled in config.
+func ChromaStylesCSS(opts ChromaStylesOptions) (string, error) {
+	name := strings.ToLower(opts.Style)
+	if !slices.Contains(styles.Names(), name) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid style: %s", name)
+	}
+	var chromaStyle *chroma.Style
+	if opts.Mode != "" {
+		var mode chroma.Mode
+		switch opts.Mode {
+		case "light":
+			mode = chroma.Light
+		case "dark":
+			mode = chroma.Dark
+		default:
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid mode: %s", opts.Mode)
+		}
+
+		chromaStyle = styles.GetForMode(name, mode)
+		if chromaStyle.Mode() != mode {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a %q mode", name, opts.Mode)
+		}
+	} else {
+		chromaStyle = styles.Get(name)
+	}
+	builder := chromaStyle.Builder()
+	if opts.HighlightStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineHighlight, opts.HighlightStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbers, opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersTableStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbersTable, opts.LineNumbersTableStyle)
+	}
+	style, err := builder.Build()
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+
+	options := []html.Option{
+		html.WithCSSComments(!opts.OmitClassComments),
+	}
+	if !opts.ModeSelector {
+		// Only needed for the shared-scope overlay; modeSelector
+		// gives each mode its own scope and makes this redundant.
+		options = append(options, html.WithCustomCSS(chromaCSSOverrides(style)))
+	}
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	if err := html.New(options...).WriteCSS(&buf, style); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	css := buf.String()
+	if opts.ModeSelector {
+		// Scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+		// This allows generating both light and dark stylesheets and toggling
+		// them with a parent class on the page.
+		// There's no upstream option for this (I think), so do string replacements for now.
+		// TODO(bep) upstream option for this.
+		var prefix string
+		switch style.Mode() {
+		case chroma.Light:
+			prefix = ".light "
+		case chroma.Dark:
+			prefix = ".dark "
+		default:
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a light or dark mode", style.Name)
+		}
+		replacer := strings.NewReplacer(
+			".bg {", prefix+".bg {",
+			".chroma ", prefix+".chroma ",
+		)
+		css = replacer.Replace(css)
+	}
+
+	return css, nil
+}
+
+// chromaCSSOverrides re-emits leaf token colors that Chroma's minifier drops
+// because they equal the style's default foreground (the .chroma color). Without
+// modeSelector scoping, a paired light/dark stylesheet shares the same .chroma
+// scope, and the light sheet's explicit rule (e.g. .chroma .nx) would otherwise
+// leak into dark mode, since an explicit declaration beats inheritance.
+func chromaCSSOverrides(style *chroma.Style) map[chroma.TokenType]string {
+	bg := style.Get(chroma.Background)
+	m := make(map[chroma.TokenType]string)
+	for tt := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if tt == chroma.Background || !style.Has(tt) || !chromaLeafToken(tt) {
+			continue
+		}
+		entry := style.Get(tt)
+		if !entry.Sub(bg).IsZero() || !entry.Colour.IsSet() {
+			continue
+		}
+		if css := html.StyleEntryToCSS(chroma.StyleEntry{Colour: entry.Colour}); css != "" {
+			m[tt] = css
+		}
+	}
+	return m
+}
+
+func chromaLeafToken(tt chroma.TokenType) bool {
+	for other := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if other != tt && (other.Category() == tt || other.SubCategory() == tt) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}

title: common/hugo: Include aom, dav1d, and libavif in commands/env output

judge.reasoning: Patch A does what the issue asks. It adds libavif v1.4.1, aom v3.14.1 and dav1d 1.5.3 next to libwebp in GetDependencyListNonGo, and notes that these versions must stay in sync with the genwebp and genavif Makefiles. Its unit test reads the version variables from those Makefiles and asserts each formatted dependency appears in the output. That test fails before the change and also catches later drift, which is a real check rather than a tautology. Its testscript checks the exact version strings in `hugo env` output. Patch B routes the versions through a new warpc.GetWASMDeps(), which makes common/hugo import internal/warpc. That is a new cross-package dependency from a low-level common package into an internal subsystem, with some risk of import cycles or heavier coupling. It also adds a KaTeX entry the issue did not ask for, with a hardcoded version that nothing checks against js/package.json. It reformats unrelated code in warpc.go (dispatcher closures, WithImportResolver), which obscures the fix. Its constants are still hand-maintained with only 'keep in sync' comments, and its testscript checks only module paths, not versions, so it would not catch wrong versions. A is narrower, lower-risk, and better tested.

title: resources/jsconfig: Address VS Code linting notice in jsconfig.json

judge.reasoning:
The lint fires because a `paths` target is not relative while `baseUrl` is unset. TypeScript wants targets to start with `./` or `../`.

Patch B fixes this at the root. Every target computed by `filepath.Rel` gets normalized to start with `./` or `../`. So `*` becomes `./*`, a subdirectory root becomes `./c/*`, and `../d/*` is left as is. The meaning of the mapping is kept: bare imports still resolve against the assets dir and the other source roots, so editor resolution keeps working.

Patch A just skips the source root equal to `dir`. That has three problems:
(1) It removes the self-mapping. In the common case (only the assets root) `Build` now returns nil and no jsconfig mapping is produced, so the editor can no longer resolve bare imports such as `imp1/index.js` from assets. That is a functional regression, not a fix.
(2) It does not handle source roots that are subdirectories of `dir`. Those still yield non-relative targets like `c/*`, which trigger the same lint.
(3) It hides the symptom by removing the mapping rather than correcting its format.

On tests, Patch B adds a unit test covering the parent (`../`), same (`./*`) and child (`./c/*`) cases. It also adds an integration test checking that the generated `assets/jsconfig.json` contains `./*` and that the JS build still resolves the bare import. Patch A's test only asserts a nil config, which encodes the regression.

The scope of both patches is comparable. Patch B's helper is small and clearly documented.

title: Panic when deleting a directory in static when server is running

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the root cause the same way. They replace the stat-dependent, directory-only `Contains` check with a `ReverseLookup`-based check. That check still classifies events for deleted mount roots and covers single-file mounts, so static events go back to the static syncer instead of the partial rebuild.

The differences are in error handling and tests:

- **Error handling.** Patch B calls `panic(err)` when `ReverseLookup` returns an error. That adds a new panic path to file-event classification in the running server, which is the kind of crash the issue reports. Patch A ignores the error and returns false, which is safer for a classification helper.
- **Fallback case.** Patch A also adds a `ComponentFolderStatic` case to the `processPartialFileEvents` switch. This is a defensive fallback rather than the fix itself. It could quietly drop a misrouted static event, but since the static syncer owns those events anyway, the risk is low and it prevents the reported panic outright.
- **Tests.** Patch A adds two server testscripts that reproduce the reported scenario end-to-end: deleting a mounted static directory and deleting a single-file static mount while the server runs, then asserting nothing is written to stderr. Patch B adds a focused unit test of `IsStatic` and `IsContent` after removing mount roots, plus a single-file mount check. That test is precise and would fail before the fix, but it does not exercise the server event path where the panic happened.

Overall, Patch A is more robust, with no new panic and a defensive switch case, and its tests reproduce the issue directly.

title: related: Add option to tokenize headings

judge.reasoning:
Patch B is the more correct fix.

**Patch B**
- Keeps the existing exact `FragmentKeyword` identifiers and adds heading-word tokens as a separate `fragmentTokenKeyword` type. A word can therefore never collide with a fragment ID, and non-heading fragments such as definition terms keep exact matching, exactly as the issue's documentation says.
- Tokenization strips HTML tags from sanitized titles, unescapes entities, honors `ToLower`, and preserves combining marks.
- It walks all headings, including nested ones, and dedupes words per document so `cardinalityThreshold` counts documents correctly.
- It extends `applyFilter` to work with tokens.
- It adds the requested docs entry.
- Tests:
  - a unit test for keyword generation and tokenization;
  - a config decode test;
  - an integration test that runs with tokenize both true and false, checking `HeadingsFiltered`, `cardinalityThreshold` pruning of 'introduction', and that definition-term refs still match.

**Patch A has a functional bug in `applyFilter`**
- Tokenized words are created via `stringToKeyword`, which yields `StringKeyword`.
- `searchDate` only collects filter terms when `kw.(FragmentKeyword)` succeeds, so `ff.words` is never populated.
- As a result, heading filtering silently does nothing when `tokenize` and `applyFilter` are combined, and its own ApplyFilter test should not pass as written.

**Other problems in Patch A**
- It replaces heading identifiers with tokens (`continue`), dropping exact-ID matching for headings. This breaks front-matter references to heading IDs in tokenized indices.
- It does not strip HTML tags from heading titles.
- It goes beyond the ask by applying `Tokenize` to all basic string indices and adding an unrequested `MinTokenLength` option. This increases risk and behavioral surface.
- It adds no documentation.
- It includes whitespace churn in existing tests.

issue_md:
See <https://discourse.gohugo.io/t/related-posts-based-on-heading/57467>.

I suggest using the name `tokenize`, documented as follows:

> (`bool`) Whether to split multi-word values into individual keywords for indexing and matching. Currently applies to heading titles in indices of type `fragments`; non-heading fragments such as definition terms continue to use exact-identifier matching regardless of this setting. This increases index size in proportion to the average number of words per heading; use `cardinalityThreshold` to prune common words and reduce build time. Default is `false`.

title: panic: slice bounds out of range in contentNodeShifter.Delete when removing draft pages from a multilingual taxonomy

judge.reasoning:
The production code in both patches is essentially the same fix, and it addresses the root cause. The old `contentNodes` branch shrank `v` with `append(v[:i], v[i+1:]...)` while ranging over it. That produces the reported 'slice bounds out of range [5:4]' once more than one node is removed, and it also mutated the backing array shared with the tree. Both patches build a separate `remaining` slice and change the `Shifter` interface to return the updated value. Both store that value back via `tree.Insert` in `delete` and `DeleteFuncRaw`, and both apply the same fix to `DeleteFunc`. The code differences are minor. A avoids reassigning `v` in the default case, which is slightly cleaner. B preallocates `remaining` and adds a comment explaining why the input must not be mutated. Neither difference matters for correctness.

The tests are where the patches differ. A's test calls the shifter directly with a stub node type. It covers multiple non-adjacent deletions, which would panic before the fix, plus the all-deleted and none-deleted cases. B's tests are broader and closer to the reported failure:
- They check that the input slice is not mutated, which is the aliasing hazard.
- They cover a nested `contentNodesMap` inside `contentNodes`.
- Most importantly, they exercise the full `NodeShiftTree`. The test deletes the same key across several dimensions in sequence and confirms the tree holds exactly the surviving nodes after each step. That is the multilingual production-build scenario from the issue, and it also checks that the new store-back logic in `delete` is correct.
- They test `DeleteFuncRaw` with adjacent deletions, which also reveals the skipped-element bug in the old `DeleteFunc`.

Because B's tests verify both the panic fix and the new write-back behaviour at the tree level, B is the stronger patch overall.

issue_md:
### What version of Hugo are you using?

Reproduced on both:

```
hugo v0.159.1-86c7d3afacab79dc53325602d77ef884b7570268+extended darwin/arm64
hugo v0.164.0+extended+withdeploy darwin/arm64
```

### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release?

Yes (0.164.0).

### What did you expect to see?

A production build (no `-D`) of a multilingual site containing draft pages completes.

### What did you see instead?

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [5:4]

goroutine 37 [running]:
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*contentNodeShifter).Delete(0x..., {0x..., 0x...}, {0x2, 0x0, 0x0})
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_contentnodeshifter.go:48 +0x5f4
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree.(*NodeShiftTree[...]).delete(0x..., {0x..., 0x35})
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree/nodeshifttree.go:165 +0x84
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree.(*NodeShiftTree[...]).Delete(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree/nodeshifttree.go:107
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*allPagesAssembler).createAllPages.func1-range1(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go:106 +0xa4
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*allPagesAssembler).createAllPages(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go:138 +0x168
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*HugoSites).assemble(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/hugo_sites_build.go:345 +0x41c
```

The `0x35` in `delete(..., {…, 0x35})` is 53, exactly the byte length of the key being removed (`/blog/` plus a 47-character slug).

### Only on the page-removal path

`hugo -D` (drafts included) builds fine. The panic appears only when a page is *removed* from the tree, which makes it invisible in local preview and fatal only in production.

A **future `publishDate`** panics identically. Setting `[_build] render = "never"` / `list = "never"` on the same pages avoids it entirely — consistent with those pages never being added to the tree, so nothing is deleted.

### What I ruled out

Site: 8 languages, ~1,490 pages per language, ~11,455 content files, `categories` taxonomy.

- **Not a regression.** 0.159.1 and 0.164.0 behave identically.
- **Not the number of drafts.** 96 draft pages build fine; 16 panic.
- **Not slug length.** The panicking key was 47 chars, but renaming an unrelated post to exactly 47 chars builds fine.
- **Not the slug.** Renaming the offending page does not help.
- **Not byte layout.** Deleting a front-matter line, or adding a blank one, still panics.

Swapping page *content* at a fixed path isolates it to **front matter**. Changing `categories = ["Airport Operations"]` on the offending page to any other value clears the panic — and so does moving a *different* page out of that same category while leaving the offending one alone. So the trigger is combinatorial: some particular set of pages being deleted from one taxonomy term corrupts the shifter, rather than any single page being malformed.

### Reproducer

I have not managed to minimise it, and I want to be upfront about that. Synthetic multilingual sites (8 languages, 12 blog + 200 glossary pages sharing one taxonomy term, varying draft counts) do **not** reproduce, so something else in the real tree is required. The affected repository is private.

I am happy to run patches or instrumented builds against the real site and report back, which may be faster than guessing at a minimal case.

title: Add resources.Publish

judge.reasoning:
Both patches add the same core change: a `Publish(r resource.Resource) (resource.Resource, error)` function in `tpl/resources`, registered via `AddMethodMapping`. It type-asserts to `resource.Source`, calls `Publish()` and returns the resource. That resolves the issue's ask in both cases, so correctness is effectively equal.

B adds an explicit nil check with a clearer message, and prefixes its errors with `resources.Publish:`. A would still fail gracefully on nil because the type assertion fails, but its error would read `<nil> can not be published`, which is less helpful. This is a minor craft gain for B.

Testing is where the patches differ meaningfully. A's single test only covers `minify | resources.Publish` and never exercises `js.Build`, the exact pipeline in the issue. B's tests cover:
- plain `resources.Get`, `minify`, `js.Build`, `resources.FromString` and a copied page-bundle resource, checking both the returned resource's properties and the published files on disk;
- the error path for passing a Page;
- the error path for a nil resource from a missing asset.

One caveat: B's assertion `p: p.txt|` for the copied bundle resource relies on naming behaviour I can't verify from the diff, so that test carries slight risk. B's docs are neutral scope that adds no risk.

Overall B is the stronger patch, mainly for test coverage of the issue's actual scenario and its edge cases, plus slightly better error handling.

title: Upgrade to Go 1.27

judge.reasoning:
Both patches make the same core changes: CI matrix, CircleCI images, go.mod, Dockerfile GO_VERSION, regenerated PNG goldens, and the synced template packages. That sync covers the CVE brace/regexp fix in transition.go, the delimiter-aware node String/writeTo, the stringer regeneration, the doc updates, and the new upstream tests. Both also handle the Go 1.27 json/v2 change that surfaces ErrShutdown from the warpc input loop.

Patch B fixes the warpc problem at its source. In inputJSON it records that the shutdown was self-initiated and returns nil. It adds a targeted unit test, TestDispatcherInputJSONClosedPipe, covering both the expected close and an unexpected close; that test would fail without the fix. Patch A instead filters ErrShutdown at the Wait call site. It also adds a global mutex around the wazero compilation cache, citing a placeholder "<link>", without explaining or testing it.

Patch B raises SkipGoldenTests to Go 1.27 alongside the regenerated PNG goldens, which keeps the golden tests consistent. Patch A changes the goldens but leaves the threshold at 26. Patch B also adds a Hugo-level integration test for the JS regexp escaping CVE, which shows the security fix reaches Hugo's own rendering.

Patch A carries a lot of unrelated churn that adds risk or obscures the change:
- It replaces cmp.Or with a new herrors.Or for no stated reason.
- It rewrites the vectorstores filter error handling to panic per filter, which changes behaviour.
- It strips debug code from the integration test builder.
- It simplifies post_publish and adds lint-ignore comments in allconfig.
- It bumps Alpine to 3.24.
- It reintroduces non-gofmt formatting across many test files, removing 145 lines from tests.

Patch A's improvements to the fork script and its CopyDir skip fix are useful tooling, but they go beyond the issue and count as neutral. Overall, Patch B is the more focused and better-tested fix.

title: templates.Defer: identical block bodies in different output formats share one escaping mode, chosen non-deterministically per build

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the root cause the same way. They fold the owner's escaping regime (IsPlainText) into the deferred-template hash. That separates HTML and plain-text registrations while keeping same-format sharing, as the issue's constraint asks. Patch A uses equal-length "html:"/"text:" prefixes; Patch B uses fmt.Sprintf("%t:%s"). Both are collision-safe.

Patch A also covers a path B does not: deferred blocks inside partial-decorator bodies (handleWithPartial). There a fresh context is created for the internal decorator template, so `c.t` is the decorator rather than the real owning template. A threads `deferOwner` and the shared `deferNodes` into that context. As a result, the escaping regime and registration come from the actual owner, and A adds a test for the plain-text case. B's `c.t.D.IsPlainText` would read the decorator template's flag in that case, which may be wrong.

On tests, A is clearly stronger:
- It builds the reproduction 20 times with exact-content assertions. This reliably fails before the fix, given the issue's roughly 65/35 split.
- B builds once. Before the fix, a single build always gets one of the two files wrong, so B's test would also fail, but A's loop better guards against the nondeterminism.
- A adds a regression test that same-format identical blocks still share one execution, which is the issue's stated constraint.
- A adds a test for the prefix-collision edge.

A's extra decorator change adds some risk, but it is coherent and tested. Overall A is the more complete and better-verified fix.

### What version of Hugo are you using (`hugo version`)?

### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes. ```text hugo v0.165.0-76a5e1880ab46688155b02e99bab9be2a6134492+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-08-12T14:26:28Z VendorInfo=gohugoio ``` Over one run of 40 consecutive builds of the unchanged reproduction site below with that binary, 28 builds published the wrong value in `public/index.html` and 12 published the wrong value in `public/index.txt`. All 40 exited 0, and none printed a warning or an error. ### Summary When two templates belonging to different output formats contain byte-identical `templates.Defer` block bodies, both blocks do execute, each with its own correct output-format context. What they share is the escaping applied inside the block, and which of the two escaping modes survives changes from build to build of an unchanged site. On every build exactly one of the two outputs is therefore wrong: either an HTML page publishes a value raw that it escapes correctly a few characters earlier outside the block, or a plain-text page receives HTML entities. ### Reproduction Three files in an empty directory. No content, no modules, no external tooling. `hugo.toml`: ```toml baseURL = 'https://example.org/' title = 'defer probe' disableKinds = ['page', 'section', 'taxonomy', 'term', 'RSS', 'sitemap', 'robotsTXT'] [outputFormats.probe] mediaType = 'text/plain' baseName = 'index' isPlainText = true [outputs] home = ['html', 'probe'] ``` `layouts/home.html`: ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` `layouts/home.probe.txt`, byte-identical to `layouts/home.html` (both md5 `c921197a9c8637852e38d94a0352359d`): ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` `OUT[...]` interpolates the value outside the deferred block, `IN[...]` interpolates the same value inside it. Then run `hugo` several times without changing anything, and look at `public/index.html` and `public/index.txt` after each run. ### What happens Two consecutive runs of the same command on the unchanged site, pasted verbatim: ```text $ hugo --logLevel info Start building sites … hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z assemble duration 0s INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat html duration 1.3703ms INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat probe duration 509.5µs INFO build: step render pages 2 content 0 duration 1.8798ms INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 1.7766ms INFO build: step postProcess duration 0s INFO build: duration 4.171ms │ EN ──────────────────┼──── Pages │ 2 Paginator pages │ 0 Non-page files │ 0 Static files │ 0 Processed images │ 0 Aliases │ 0 Cleaned │ 0 Total in 12 ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[&] ``` ```text $ hugo --logLevel info Start building sites … hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio INFO build: step process substep collect files 0 files_total 0 pagesources_total 0 resourcesources_total 0 duration 513.8µs INFO build: step process duration 513.8µs INFO build: step assemble duration 0s INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat html duration 517.9µs INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat probe duration 517.2µs INFO build: step render pages 2 content 0 duration 1.0351ms INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 2.0736ms INFO build: step postProcess duration 0s INFO build: duration 3.6225ms │ EN public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[<b>&] ``` In the first run the HTML page publishes `&` raw inside the block, a few characters after escaping the same value correctly outside it. In the second run the plain-text page receives `<b>&`. Nothing changed between the two runs. Quantified over builds of the unchanged site, each build a separate one-shot `hugo` invocation: | Hugo version | builds | `index.html` published raw `&` inside the block | `index.txt` published `<b>&` inside the block | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | v0.164.0, fresh copy of the site per build | 40 | 25 | 15 | | v0.164.0, fresh copy of the site per build, second run | 40 | 23 | 17 | | v0.165.0, fresh copy of the site per build | 40 | 26 | 14 | | v0.165.0, fresh copy of the site per build, second run | 40 | 28 | 12 | | v0.164.0, repeated builds in one directory | 12 | 8 | 4 | | v0.165.0, repeated builds in one directory | 8 | 5 | 3 | In all 180 of those builds the two output formats carried the *same* string inside the block, so exactly one of the two published files was wrong every time; outside the block the value was escaped correctly for its format in every build. ### What I expected Each format's deferred block rendered under that format's own escaping — `IN[<b>&]` in `public/index.html` and `IN[&]` in `public/index.txt` — and the same result on every build of an unchanged site. The documentation says "The output format, site, and language will be the same, even if the execution is deferred." The output-format *context* does hold up, as the identity-token control below shows; it is the escaping regime that does not follow the output format. ### Controls All of these were run at both v0.164.0 and v0.165.0. **The block really does execute once per output format.** Adding `{{ warnf "DEFER-EXEC-%d" math.Counter }}` to the start of the still byte-identical block body logs two executions in every build: ```text WARN DEFER-EXEC-1 WARN DEFER-EXEC-2 INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 1.7497ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[&] ``` So this is not one rendering substituted into two files; it is two renderings sharing one escaping mode. **Different `key` values do not separate them.** With `"KH"` in `layouts/home.html` and `"KT"` in `layouts/home.probe.txt`, the block bodies still byte-identical, the escaping stayed shared and kept flipping: 36 builds, 22 with the HTML page wrong and 14 with the plain-text page wrong. **Different block body text does separate them, stably.** Changing the body to `INH[{{ .v }}]` in the HTML template and `INT[{{ .v }}]` in the plain-text template gives the correct per-format result in 36 of 36 builds, with no flip: `INH[<b>&]` in `public/index.html` and `INT[&]` in `public/index.txt`. **The per-format context inside the block is correct.** With the body still byte-identical in both templates, but carrying an output-format identity token next to the value: ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ (index page.AlternativeOutputFormats 0).Name }}|{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` With exactly two formats configured the single alternative names the *other* one, so `IN[probe|...]` marks the execution that produced the HTML page and `IN[html|...]` the one that produced the plain-text page. That token was correct in 36 of 36 builds, while the escaping of the value beside it in the very same body was shared and flipped across those builds: ```text public/index.html OUT[<b>&]IN[probe|&] public/index.txt OUT[&]IN[html|&] public/index.html OUT[<b>&]IN[probe|<b>&] public/index.txt OUT[&]IN[html|<b>&] ``` ### Where this appears to come from Offered as a lead from reading the source, not as an instrumented finding. `tpl/tplimpl/templatetransform.go`, `handleWith` (v0.164.0, function at line 409) registers the extracted block under a hash of the block body alone, at lines 450-459: ```go inner := withNode.List.CopyList() s := inner.String() ... innerHash := hashing.XxHashFromStringHexEncoded(s) deferredID := tpl.HugoDeferredTemplatePrefix + innerHash ... c.deferNodes[deferredID] = inner ``` Nothing about the owning template, its output format or its media type enters that identifier, so two templates in different output formats with the same body produce the same `deferredID`. `tpl/tplimpl/templatestore.go`, `addDeferredTemplate` (v0.164.0, function at line 916) then keeps only the first registration under that name, and the first owner fixes the parse namespace for whoever comes later: ```go if _, found := t.templatesByPath.Get(name); found { return nil } ... if owner.D.IsPlainText { prototype := t.tns.parseText ... } else { prototype := t.tns.parseHTML ... } ``` That is exactly the escaping regime the two output formats disagree about, and the loser silently inherits the winner's. Which owner gets there first looks order-dependent. `transformTemplates` (function at line 1916) reaches the registrations by ranging `s.templates()` at line 1937, and that iterator's inner loop at line 1784 ranges a `map[nodeKey]*TemplInfo` — the value type of `treeMain`, declared at line 447 — whose iteration order Go randomizes per run. I found no sort on that path. One contrast worth noting: the sibling transform in the same file, `handleWithPartial` (function at line 324), hashes the owning template's name into its identifier at line 335 — `hashing.XxHashFromStringHexEncoded(c.t.Name() + withNodeInnerString)` — while the older defer path does not. I checked the implicated files at v0.164.0, v0.165.0 and master `7b5199fdeff7d7682e9f979f468d55bc7b67b934`: `tpl/tplimpl/templatestore.go`, `tpl/templates/templates.go` and `tpl/template.go` are byte-identical at all three, and `tpl/tplimpl/templatetransform.go` differs at master only outside this path — the `handleWith` lines quoted above are unchanged there, at 405-414. ### A constraint on any fix Hashing the owning template's name into the deferred identifier, the way `handleWithPartial` does, would break something the documentation promises for `key`: "This will, combined with a hash of the template content, be used as a cache key." Two *different layouts of the same output format* with identical bodies and one shared key share a single execution today, and that is worth keeping — at both versions, on a variant of the site above reduced to one output format and with the `page` kind enabled plus one content file, so that `single.html` renders at all, I measured a single `DEFER-EXEC-1` for a `home.html` and a `single.html` written that way, with both pages publishing the shared result. Separating registrations by the property that actually differs here — the owner's `IsPlainText`, or its output format — would fix the escaping while leaving that documented same-format sharing untouched. ### Related, not duplicates - #7774, fixed by #8462 ("Fixes #7774", merged 2021-04-23): per-build nondeterminism in output-format template lookup for shortcodes. Same failure shape, different subsystem, and it predates `templates.Defer`. - #13236: two empty deferred blocks *in the same template* collided on the identifier `__hdeferred/cafc7706cee4572b` and panicked; closed as completed. That is the same body-only identifier, in a different situation — the collision there is inside one template, and the cross-output-format escaping consequence does not come up. I did not find an existing report covering byte-identical `templates.Defer` bodies across output formats. ### What I did not establish - **Which registration wins in any individual build.** I inferred the winner from the escaping in the published output; I did not instrument the running binary to observe the registration. - **Platform generality.** Everything above was measured on one machine, Windows 11, amd64 extended builds. Whether the split differs on another platform or core count is unmeasured. - **Two non-plain-text formats sharing a body.** The escaping observable needs an `isPlainText` format paired with an HTML one, so two HTML-ish formats sharing a body were not tested and the reach across format combinations is unknown.
